notes: Phobos Agriculture crops (Agriculture 0.40.0): what a Firstlight rack grows, what each planting needs and what a harvest gives. One entry per crop; the entry's name is what a saved planting stores, so a published crop is frozen (frozen-crops.json): change one by adding a crop beside it. Every crop conserves mass: water + nutrient + 0.4 x carbon - vapour = final - seed, where 0.4 x carbon is the carbon dioxide taken in less the oxygen given off (CH2O, 30 g per mol of carbon). Growth times are authored gameplay balance, far shorter than real cultivation; see docs/development/agriculture-research.md for the NASA and ESA sources and their limits. The items section names the crop items the code builds from the materials pack, their text and what eating one gives.

potato.notes: Seed potato into a five-kilogram cohort over 96 hours at 0.75 kW. A harvest keeps one seed potato and gives 0.4 kg raw portions for the Hearth-2. Unchanged since Agriculture 0.2.0.

lettuce.notes: One seed packet into 1.2 kg of lettuce over 48 hours at 0.4 kW, cut as 0.25 kg portions eaten as they are. Unchanged since Agriculture 0.2.0.

lettuce-seed.notes: Lettuce left to bolt for seed: one packet into four packets over 96 hours. An authored seed cycle, separate from the food crop.

wheat.notes: Dwarf wheat (Agriculture 0.41.0): one 50 g packet of seed wheat into a 1.4 kg cohort over 84 hours at 1.2 kW. A harvest keeps one packet back for the next planting and gives one 0.4 kg portion of grain; the rest, about 0.95 kg, is straw. Authored in the ratios NASA Kennedy Space Center's Biomass Production Chamber found against potato: a slightly shorter cycle (77 to 86 days against 90 to 105), the most light, about 30 to 40% of the plant edible, and a ripe crop that is mostly dry matter. See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md; the hours are authored gameplay balance.

tomato.notes: Dwarf tomato (Agriculture 0.42.0): one 5 g seed packet into a 5 kg plant, first ripe after 64 hours at 0.7 kW. A ripe plant can be picked three times, up to three 0.25 kg portions a pick; each pick sets growth back by the share of a cycle it took, so the plant regrows that fruit from the same budget (about ten hours at full health). The final harvest takes the rest, a seed packet kept from the fruit and the vine as residue. Ratios after NASA Kennedy Space Center's Biomass Production Chamber tomato: first fruit at about two thirds of potato's cycle, fruit picked as it ripened over the last quarter, about half the dry matter in fruit, and ripe fruit 94.5% water (USDA). See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md; hours, picks and yields are authored gameplay balance.

soybean.notes: Soybean (Agriculture 0.42.0): one 30 g seed packet into a 0.9 kg stand over 90 hours at 0.65 kW. A harvest keeps one packet back and gives one 0.25 kg portion of dry beans; the rest, about 0.62 kg, is straw. Ratios after NASA Kennedy Space Center's Biomass Production Chamber soybean: about potato's cycle (90 to 97 days), less light than wheat, about a third of the dry matter in seed, and seed of 37% protein and 20% fat (dry basis). See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md; hours and yields are authored gameplay balance.

flax.notes: Fibre flax (Agriculture 0.45.0): one 10 g packet of flax seed sown dense into a 1.6 kg stand over 90 hours at 0.9 kW. Pulled at yellow ripeness and retted, a harvest gives four 0.25 kg bundles of flax straw for the B2 to scutch into the game's clean scrap cloth, keeps one packet of linseed back for the next sowing, and leaves about 0.59 kg of roots, leaves and bolls as residue. Fibre flax takes about 90 to 100 days from sowing to pulling; the hours, light and yields are authored gameplay balance. See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md.

sugar-beet.notes: Sugar beet (Agriculture 0.46.0): one 20 g packet of seed into a 6 kg stand over 140 hours at 0.8 kW. A harvest gives nine 0.5 kg roots for the B2 to extract sugar from, or for a Phobos Manufacturing fermenter, keeps one packet back, and leaves about 1.48 kg of leaves and crowns as residue. Roots run 75 to 80% water and 15 to 20% sucrose (University of California, Davis, Sugar Beet as a Biofuel Feedstock); a field crop takes 150 to 200 days. The hours, light and yields are authored gameplay balance. See docs/development/agriculture-crop-expansion.md.

co2Response.notes: How the rack's room carbon dioxide speeds growth (Agriculture 0.43.0): points of (CO2 partial pressure in kPa, growth factor). The factor multiplies growth per hour and per kWh; budgets per kilogram are unchanged, so an enriched room shortens the cycle and its energy. At a normal cabin pressure 0.1 kPa is about 1,000 ppm. Source findings: NASA Kennedy Space Center ran its Biomass Production Chamber at 1,000 or 1,200 ppm and found C3 crop photosynthesis saturating between about 1,000 and 1,500 ppm (NASA/TM-2003-211184); Utah State University found wheat seed yield 13 to 40% higher at 1,000 to 1,200 ppm than at ambient, falling 15 to 22% at 2,500 ppm and 37% by 10,000 ppm (Grotenhuis and Bugbee 1997; Reuveni and Bugbee 1997; Bugbee and colleagues 1994). Authored: +20% at 0.1 kPa and +25% at 0.15 kPa, back to the historic rate by 0.5 kPa and slower above; no penalty below 0.04 kPa (a room with no CO2 still stops growth, as before). Every shipped crop is a C3 plant and shares the curve.

growth.notes: Where and how crops grow, and how a W2 feeds them (Agriculture 0.55.0). Authored gameplay limits, not plant physiology. Every figure may be left out and then takes the mod's default. Player files and add-ons may change any of them; an entry under crops gives one crop its own room. nutrientTargetKg is the nutrient a W2 keeps in each rack it feeds (a rack holds at most 0.5 kg). feedStrengthKgPerKg is the nutrient each kilogram of water the pump moves can carry, fresh or recirculated: at 0.01, topping a rack up by 0.1 kg moves 10 kg of water.

room.notes: The room every crop grows in: temperature in C, pressure in kPa. The ceiling is 31 C (owner decision, 5 October 2026; 26 C until Agriculture 0.54.0, then 30 C): crops of the game's day are presumed engineered ones, and a ship's rooms sit at about 25 C or a little above.

stress.notes: A crop shrugs off graceHours of stress (no light, no water, a room outside its limits), then loses health per further hour: healthLossPerHour in a room that suits it, healthLossPerHourOutside in one that does not, healthLossPerHourNoAir in one with no air. Health runs from 1 to 0. plantWaterKg is the water a rack needs before a crew order plants in it.

misting.notes: Misting a crop in a room too hot for it (Agriculture 0.59.0), switched on per rack. Up to maxCoolingC above the crop's ceiling, with water enough, the crop counts as in a suitable room; hotter, or short of water, heat damage is multiplied by damageShareBeyond while it mists. It takes waterKgPerHourPerC for each degree it covers and never draws the reservoir below reserveKg. The water evaporates: the room's air loses 2.45 MJ per kg and the water goes to a linked water tank, or is lost. The rate is an authored estimate of the evaporation that holds a rack's canopy that much below the air, not a measured figure. A crop's own entry under crops may set its own maxCoolingC.

PhobosVerdemorrowTomatoes.notes: Eaten fresh, like lettuce: a quarter kilogram of tomatoes is little food energy.

PhobosVerdemorrowHearthSoybeans.notes: A bowl from 0.25 kg of dry beans: about three potato portions of food energy and far more protein, so it satisfies for longer.

PhobosVerdemorrowFlaxStraw.notes: Not food: retted flax straw for the B2 to scutch.

PhobosVerdemorrowSugarBeets.notes: Not eaten raw here: roots for B2 sugar or a fermenter.

PhobosVerdemorrowBeetSugar.notes: 70 g of white sugar, about 280 kcal: a little food, not a meal.

PhobosVerdemorrowHearthFlatbread.notes: The game's own prepared-meal values (food 9, satiety 5): a loaf from 0.4 kg of grain is about four potato portions of food energy.
